=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Before the issues

- **The "FINAL / not to be re-opened" label is the Seller's claim, not an agreed fact.** Before treating any position as closed, confirm with Wattlebridge principals what, if anything, was actually agreed. Nothing in the package records Buyer sign-off.
- **The "market context" preamble is advocacy.** The ranges it cites (10–20% cap, ~1% basket, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge qualifiers) are the Seller's framing. Buyer-knowledge qualifiers in particular are not a neutral market norm. Benchmark against our own precedent and any W&I underwriter's requirements.
- **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its cover note.** The letter confirms that the Bluefen consent is not obtained, Riverlark is not repaid, Ironquay payment and assignment are not evidenced, bonuses are omitted from funds flow, and the DD-006 incident is unresolved. Several items described as "addressed" or "adequate" are open.
- **The privacy timing is overdue.** The letter is dated 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026, more than 30 days later. This matters for the Privacy Act NDB assessment window (see SPA-N-012).

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims. Via cl 12.3 and "Fundamental", the cap extends to everything.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A higher general cap, opening at 40–50% and prepared to settle around 30%. Alternatively, 20% if a W&I policy sits above it.
  - The cap limited strictly to general warranties.
  - Fundamental warranties capped at 100% of price.
  - Tax and specific indemnities outside the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as drafted. Counter at 40% for general warranties, with separate caps for the other categories.
- **Reason:** A 20% cap is only acceptable if it applies to general warranties alone, and the Seller's drafting applies it to all claims.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000 (~1.04% of price), deductible so only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - De minimis around AUD 10,000.
  - Related or series claims aggregated for de minimis purposes.
  - Basket around 0.5% (AUD 120,000) on a tipping (first-dollar) basis.
  - Thresholds not applying to fundamental, tax or specific-indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter.
- **Reason:** A deductible basket of over 1%, with no aggregation of related claims, lets the Seller keep up to AUD 250k of genuine loss and lets claims be split below the de minimis.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. Under cl 12.3/13, "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - 24 months for general warranties, covering two full audit cycles.
  - Tax: at least the ATO amendment period plus 6 months, typically 5–7 years.
  - Fundamental warranties: the NSW Limitation Act period (6 years contract, 12 years deed).
- **Recommendation:** 18 months could be accepted for general warranties if it is clearly confined to them. Reject the "applies to all Claims" default.
- **Reason:** The default clause quietly applies an 18-month bar to tax, title and indemnity claims.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties share the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Capacity, authority, title and share-capital warranties with:
  - a cap of 100% of price;
  - no de minimis or basket;
  - no disclosure against them;
  - the statutory limitation period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** We are paying AUD 24m for the shares, so a AUD 4.8m cap on a title failure is commercially untenable.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 (limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance) apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that no limitation, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provision applies to claims arising from fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers, or Company management before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Insist.
- **Reason:** NSW courts are unlikely to enforce exclusions of fraud liability, and ACL s18 cannot be contracted out of. Still, the drafting should not invite the argument, and a carve-out is a standard W&I requirement.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of:
  - the entire data room as at 22 Sept 2026;
  - the Accounts;
  - statutory registers;
  - all public records.

  Cl 1.4 also denies any admission of materiality or of any required consent.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Only matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature, scope and effect of the matter.
  - No general data room disclosure. At most, specifically referenced documents.
  - Public records limited to named searches on a specified date.
  - No disclosure against fundamental warranties, the tax indemnity or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the general disclosures (1.1, 1.2).
- **Reason:** Blanket data room disclosure would hollow out every warranty. It would also disclose against the very risks we need indemnities for.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, *including anything discoverable* from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** A pro-sandbagging clause: Buyer knowledge, actual or constructive, does not reduce any claim.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** Constructive knowledge imputed through advisers would give the Seller a defence to almost any claim. It would also neutralise specific indemnities for known issues (Ironquay, DD-006, Bluefen).
- **Fallback, only if needed to close:** Limit to the actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, of facts they knew constituted a breach, excluding fundamental warranties, tax and indemnities.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** "Addressed". Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of a written consent. The Disclosure Letter (item 2) admits that no consent has been obtained and the cl 11.3 conditions are not evidenced.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A Condition Precedent requiring an unconditional written change-of-control consent from Bluefen, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  - Evidence that all DD-002 cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - All reasonable endeavours from the Seller.
  - The condition waivable only by the Buyer.
  - A sunset date with a Buyer termination right.
  - Ideally, a specific indemnity or price protection if Bluefen terminates or re-prices within a set period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "addressed". Make it a hard CP.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m), and a bare consent letter may not satisfy cl 11.3.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with the release "to be provided following Completion". Not repaid, and no discharge in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The facility treated as Debt on the debt-free/cash-free basis and repaid from the price at Completion under the funds flow.
  - Before Completion: a payoff letter stating the exact amount, plus executed deeds of release and discharge, with PPSR releases (and any share security released) delivered at Completion.
  - Confirmation that the cl 8.1 change-of-control does not trigger default before repayment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release.
- **Reason:** A post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning an encumbered company and holding a risk of up to AUD 3.2m. That is inconsistent with the agreed debt-free price.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 in DD-005 Completion bonuses described as "a matter for the Seller", yet not in the funds flow. Payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Bonuses and all associated on-costs (PAYG withholding, super, payroll tax, workers comp) treated as Transaction Costs or Debt-like items.
  - These amounts deducted from the price, or paid through payroll at Completion and funded by the Seller.
  - An indemnity for any shortfall.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Itemise the bonuses in the funds flow.
- **Reason:** The legal liability falls on the Company, so leaving the amounts out of the funds flow means the Buyer pays roughly AUD 420k plus on-costs.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open per DD-010) and described as "adequate". The data room has no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Before Completion: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay. Make these a CP or Completion deliverable.
  - A specific indemnity for all Loss arising from any Ironquay claim to or over the SOW3 Project Materials. This should include re-development, injunction and third-party costs.
  - The indemnity sitting outside caps, basket, disclosure and buyer knowledge, with a time limit of at least 6 years.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as inadequate.
- **Reason:** The real risk is that the Company does not own core IP, not the AUD 180k fee.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. The letter confirms:
  - about 1,240 records of personal information were sent to an unintended external address;
  - whether anyone accessed them is unknown;
  - whether notification is required is undetermined.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Pre-Completion covenants:**
    - complete the investigation;
    - finish the NDB "eligible data breach" assessment;
    - make any OAIC and individual notifications;
    - give the Buyer full information and consultation rights.
  - An urgent written update. The 30-day assessment period from 22 Sept 2026 has likely passed, so we should ask whether the assessment was completed and documented.
  - A specific indemnity, outside all limitations and disclosure, covering OAIC penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party and customer claims (including Bluefen).
  - A privacy/data warranty that is not qualified by the disclosure.
  - Consider an escrow or retention.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the characterisation.
- **Reason:** The Seller does not know the scope of the incident, so it cannot assert that it is immaterial. Unresolved NDB compliance is a regulatory exposure the Buyer would inherit.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k aggregate) described as ordinary-course. The letter does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued, and DD-008/DD-011 should be read together.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Disclosure of dates, terms, termination rights and approvals.
  - Confirmation that the renewals were not split to avoid a material-contract or conduct-of-business threshold.
  - The renewals treated as a single related matter.
  - If entered in the pre-Completion period without consent, or not in the ordinary course: Seller-borne cost, a price adjustment, or termination before Completion.
  - Conduct-of-business covenants that aggregate related contracts.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "ordinary course" without evidence.
- **Reason:** Three identical related renewals suggest threshold-splitting, and the cost sits with the Company after Completion.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Drafting that keeps separate regimes for each of:
  - general warranties;
  - fundamental warranties;
  - tax warranties and indemnity;
  - specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark, Bluefen if agreed);
  - leakage or locked-box items;
  - fraud.

  Each needs its own cap, thresholds, time limit and disclosure treatment. Limitations should apply only where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Reverse the default.
- **Reason:** This single drafting device converts every bespoke protection into a capped, time-barred, general warranty claim.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the DD-012 share register. The letter itself says this is only the source relied on and that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Fundamental warranties covering legal and beneficial ownership of 100% of the shares, free of Encumbrances, with no options, rights or convertibles outstanding.
  - Our own ASIC company extract and PPSR search, reconciled to the register and to the history of issues and transfers.
  - At Completion: the original share certificates, executed transfers, board approvals and any security releases.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone.
- **Reason:** A share register is the Seller's own record and is not conclusive of beneficial title or freedom from encumbrances.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Says these are "settled under the general regime". There is no evidence of agreement, and doing so would apply the 20% cap and 18-month limit.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:**
    - a specific pre-Completion tax indemnity, dollar-for-dollar and outside the basket;
    - capped at the price;
    - running for the ATO amendment period plus 6 months;
    - with Buyer conduct of tax claims, subject to reasonable Seller consultation.
  - **IP:**
    - IP warranties carved out as "IP fundamental" or with an extended period (3–4 years) and a higher cap;
    - backed by the Ironquay indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Treat these as open and table Buyer drafting.
- **Reason:** For a SaaS target, tax and IP are core value risks, and nothing in the package shows they were agreed on these terms.

---

## Suggested next steps
1. Confirm with principals that no positions were in fact agreed, and respond that the package is not accepted as final.
2. Send the Seller a Buyer mark-up of cl 2, 3, 6–9, 11–13 and 20, with a separate Specific Indemnities schedule and a reversed limitations default.
3. Issue urgent requests for:
   - the DD-006 NDB assessment status;
   - Bluefen cl 11.3 evidence;
   - the Riverlark payoff letter;
   - Ironquay payment proof and assignment;
   - the Sandbar contracts;
   - on-cost calculations for the bonuses.
4. Run our own ASIC and PPSR searches. If W&I insurance is contemplated, align the cap, basket and knowledge positions with the underwriter early.

This is a working analysis for the deal team. Final positions should be confirmed by supervising NSW-qualified counsel.

  - Bonuses and all associated on-costs (PAYG withholding, super, payroll tax, workers comp) treated as Transaction Costs or Debt-like items.
  - These amounts deducted from the price, or paid through payroll at Completion and funded by the Seller.
  - An indemnity for any shortfall.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Itemise the bonuses in the funds flow.
- **Reason:** The legal liability falls on the Company, so leaving the amounts out of the funds flow means the Buyer pays roughly AUD 420k plus on-costs.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open per DD-010) and described as "adequate". The data room has no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Before Completion: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay. Make these a CP or Completion deliverable.
  - A specific indemnity for all Loss arising from any Ironquay claim to or over the SOW3 Project Materials. This should include re-development, injunction and third-party costs.
  - The indemnity sitting outside caps, basket, disclosure and buyer knowledge, with a time limit of at least 6 years.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as inadequate.
- **Reason:** The real risk is that the Company does not own core IP, not the AUD 180k fee.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. The letter confirms:
  - about 1,240 records of personal information were sent to an unintended external address;
  - whether anyone accessed them is unknown;
  - whether notification is required is undetermined.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Pre-Completion covenants:**
    - complete the investigation;
    - finish the NDB "eligible data breach" assessment;
    - make any OAIC and individual notifications;
    - give the Buyer full information and consultation rights.
  - An urgent written update. The 30-day assessment period from 22 Sept 2026 has likely passed, so we should ask whether the assessment was completed and documented.
  - A specific indemnity, outside all limitations and disclosure, covering OAIC penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party and customer claims (including Bluefen).
  - A privacy/data warranty that is not qualified by the disclosure.
  - Consider an escrow or retention.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the characterisation.
- **Reason:** The Seller does not know the scope of the incident, so it cannot assert that it is immaterial. Unresolved NDB compliance is a regulatory exposure the Buyer would inherit.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k aggregate) described as ordinary-course. The letter does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued, and DD-008/DD-011 should be read together.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Disclosure of dates, terms, termination rights and approvals.
  - Confirmation that the renewals were not split to avoid a material-contract or conduct-of-business threshold.
  - The renewals treated as a single related matter.
  - If entered in the pre-Completion period without consent, or not in the ordinary course: Seller-borne cost, a price adjustment, or termination before Completion.
  - Conduct-of-business covenants that aggregate related contracts.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "ordinary course" without evidence.
- **Reason:** Three identical related renewals suggest threshold-splitting, and the cost sits with the Company after Completion.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Drafting that keeps separate regimes for each of:
  - general warranties;
  - fundamental warranties;
  - tax warranties and indemnity;
  - specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark, Bluefen if agreed);
  - leakage or locked-box items;
  - fraud.

  Each needs its own cap, thresholds, time limit and disclosure treatment. Limitations should apply only where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Reverse the default.
- **Reason:** This single drafting device converts every bespoke protection into a capped, time-barred, general warranty claim.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the DD-012 share register. The letter itself says this is only the source relied on and that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Fundamental warranties covering legal and beneficial ownership of 100% of the shares, free of Encumbrances, with no options, rights or convertibles outstanding.
  - Our own ASIC company extract and PPSR search, reconciled to the register and to the history of issues and transfers.
  - At Completion: the original share certificates, executed transfers, board approvals and any security releases.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone.
- **Reason:** A share register is the Seller's own record and is not conclusive of beneficial title or freedom from encumbrances.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Says these are "settled under the general regime". There is no evidence of agreement, and doing so would apply the 20% cap and 18-month limit.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:**
    - a specific pre-Completion tax indemnity, dollar-for-dollar and outside the basket;
    - capped at the price;
    - running for the ATO amendment period plus 6 months;
    - with Buyer conduct of tax claims, subject to reasonable Seller consultation.
  - **IP:**
    - IP warranties carved out as "IP fundamental" or with an extended period (3–4 years) and a higher cap;
    - backed by the Ironquay indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Treat these as open and table Buyer drafting.
- **Reason:** For a SaaS target, tax and IP are core value risks, and nothing in the package shows they were agreed on these terms.
